Minor Burns: Cool the burn under cool (not ice-cold) running water for 10 to 20 minutes.
Remove tight items like rings or watches before swelling starts.
Cover loosely with a sterile, non-stick bandage. Do not pop blisters.
Seek urgent medical care for large, deep, or facial/joint burns.
Minor Cuts & Scrapes: Wash hands and apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth to stop bleeding.
Rinse the wound under clean running water and wash mild soap around (not inside) deep wounds.
Apply a thin layer of plain petroleum jelly or ointment and cover with a sterile bandage.
Seek medical evaluation if bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes or if the wound is deep/dirty.
Choking (Adult - Conscious): Encourage coughing if the person can cough forcefully or speak.
If unable to speak, cough, or breathe, call emergency services immediately.
Deliver 5 back blows between the shoulder blades followed by 5 abdominal thrusts (if safe/trained to do so).
If the person becomes unresponsive, call emergency services and begin CPR.

wellness_tips: Stay hydrated throughout the day and pair routine checkup dates with calendar reminders.
Aim for consistent sleep schedules, regular movement, and balanced meals.
Keep an updated list of current medications and allergies before any doctor visit.
